Our Contact Centre & Omnichannel team is hiring several co-op students for the Winter 2027 term. We’re focused on making every interaction count by delivering faster, simpler, and smarter service experiences for our clients and frontline teams. As a Contact Centre & Omnichannel Co-op, you’ll contribute to strategic initiatives that improve client and employee experiences across the Contact Centre and broader Omnichannel ecosystem. You’ll work in a collaborative, cross-functional environment alongside business, technology, and partner teams across CIBC. Depending on business needs and your experience, you’ll support one of several focus areas, including journey mapping and process design, channel applications, channel insights, or channel data engineering. In each area, you’ll help turn ideas, data, and client needs into meaningful improvements that support lasting value.

Channel Insights: Turn channel data into actionable insights that support transaction deflection, improve digital containment, and identify friction points and opportunities across products and client journeys.

Turn information into insights - Analyze channel data to identify friction points, opportunities, and trends across products and client journeys. Help generate insights that support digital containment, transaction deflection, and improved client experiences.
Assist with data and tool development - Support the development and maintenance of data pipelines, data mapping, and internal business tools that enable reporting and self-serve access to channel insights.
Work collaboratively across teams - Partner with business, technology, and cross-functional stakeholders to support shared goals, maintain alignment, and contribute to meaningful outcomes.
Bring curiosity and perspective - Stay informed on digital capabilities, client behaviour, and market trends. Explore opportunities, challenge assumptions, and contribute ideas that help improve how we serve clients across channels.

You put our clients first. You value simple, effective, and seamless experiences, and you’re motivated by work that improves how clients interact with us across channels.

The AI & Emerging Technology Risk Oversight team, part of Global Risk Management, is an independent second-line function. We provide oversight and challenge of how Manulife manages its AI, technology, cyber, data, and emerging technology risks as the company expands its use of data and new technologies.

Manulife is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Data Risk Oversight, to build the frameworks, standards, methodologies, and tools that enable effective data risk management and oversight across the enterprise, and to provide independent challenge of the systemic and strategic data risks that shape the company's overall risk posture.

This role is distinct from the segment-level oversight performed by Information Risk Officers, who use these frameworks and tools to challenge individual business decisions and initiatives. It does not own or operate data controls, perform first-line data activities, approve initiatives, accept or own data risk, or manage remediation. These responsibilities remain with the first line and the relevant governance forums.

Position Responsibilities:
Design, maintain, and continuously improve the enterprise data risk oversight framework, standards, methodologies, and tools that enable data risk to be managed and challenged consistently across the organization.
Build the practical oversight tools, guidance, templates, and assessment approaches that segment Information Risk Officers use to perform their challenge of first-line data risk decisions.
Aggregate and analyze data risk across segments and functions to identify concentrations, themes, systemic exposures, and gaps in the enterprise risk posture.
Provide independent challenge of the overall effectiveness, consistency, and maturity of Manulife's AI and data risk program.
Set enterprise standards and oversight expectations across the data lifecycle, including data governance, quality and fitness for use, lineage and provenance, retention, minimization, and disposal.
Define enterprise standards and oversight approaches for data privacy, consent, sensitive-data classification, and access control, in coordination with Privacy, Legal, and Compliance.
Establish risk expectations and oversight approaches for third-party, shared, and AI-generated (synthetic) data, including the right to use it, its quality, its security, and whether its source is known and appropriate.
Challenge data bias, representativeness, and ethical data use at a program level, particularly for data that feeds AI, and escalate systemic concerns about potential harm, unfairness, or misuse.
Oversee enterprise data risk issues, ensuring significant and systemic weaknesses are identified, aggregated, and escalated to senior management and governance committees for timely resolution.
Define enterprise data risk metrics and key risk indicators, and produce independent reporting, thematic reviews, and cross-segment dashboards for management and committees, feeding into Board-level reporting.
Ensure the framework and oversight activities remain aligned with relevant OSFI guidance (including E-21 operational and data risk and E-23 model risk), enterprise data risk standards, and applicable privacy regimes.
Provide independent, strategic challenge on enterprise initiatives, AI use cases, and emerging technologies involving data, coordinating with the AI Model Risk, AI Technology & Cyber, and Emerging Technology teams so oversight is coordinated and non-duplicative.

10+ years of relevant experience in data risk, data governance, privacy, enterprise risk management, technology risk, internal audit, or a related discipline.

Strong understanding of the core areas of data governance, including data quality, lineage, classification, retention, privacy, consent, and access management.
Experience aggregating and analyzing risk across a large, complex organization to identify systemic themes, and familiarity with relevant OSFI guidance (including E-21 operational and data risk, E-23 model risk, B-10 third-party, and B-13 technology and cyber) and privacy laws such as PIPEDA and other global privacy rules.
Experience overseeing or challenging data used in AI, machine learning, or advanced analytics, including AI training data and synthetic data, and a good understanding of how data risk connects to model risk.
Experience preparing risk assessments, management reporting, executive presentations, and materials for governance committees.
A proven ability to challenge others constructively and influence senior leaders without direct authority.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex data and risk topics clearly to senior leaders and committees.
Strong judgment, independence, and the confidence to raise tough issues, along with the ability to juggle priorities and work quickly while keeping quality high and documentation clear.
Bilingualism (English and French) is a strong asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.
